title: Independent verification: exact enclosure of the pivot-566+554 T74 complex root behind the top pending kappa claims (no new kappa)
body:
## Independent enclosure of the pivot-566+554 T74 complex root (no new κ)

**Card:** `independent-moment` (independent-verification track, scope key `c6f2494b197df3bc3591`, chooser OS nonce `9dd43e38694b6907874fe4e993da7bf9`, priority revision 3). Scope **changed**, with the reason in `TASK.json`. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18927871. Base `ae95f60feec79897b153dba6459bb3f9fd4d7b8e`. Adds only `research/t74-k554-root-enclosure/`.

### Why this object

The selected https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1094 pricing already has independent ledger, moment, invoice and outer checks (frontier1094-emitted-ledger-seed78, selected-suppliers-de-diagnostic, pr1407-complex-moment-audit-seed39, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1735). So I applied the card's enclosure method to the pending supplier behind the highest open claims.

Every claim from https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1800 to https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1928 prices the pivot-566+554 T74 supplier. At their "free ε → 1" point, κ approaches this supplier's complex moment root. https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1928 sets b to its certified native endpoint minus 10^-10010. Until now, only the authors' own engines had certified that endpoint.

### What is checked

The inputs are the global profile `{1:1560432, 2:336336, 3:278724, 4:84912, 5:54612, 8:5328, 48:22748}`, m = 73 and W = 66304. They are pinned by Git blob and SHA-256 from `new/SPEC.json` at https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1672 (head `b8ab040d`) and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1928 (head `07e4e423`). `extract_inputs.py --check` rebuilds `INPUTS.json` byte for byte from the fetched pull refs.

The moment definitions come from the written review rather than code: native moment from `research/native-complex-moment552/PROOF.md`, conservative fallback from `notes/three-stage-cover-assembly.tex`.

The method shares no algorithm with the authors' Mercator and binary-reduction engines or with earlier audits:

- ln 2, ln 3 and ln 5 are integer combinations of ln(16/15), ln(25/24) and ln(81/80). Each of these is 2 atanh(1/k), and the verifier checks the identities exactly.
- ln 73 = ln 72 + 2 atanh(1/145).
- exp uses argument halving, a Taylor polynomial with a tail bound, and repeated squaring.
- All values are outward-rounded integers. The final comparison is exact. Undecided signs fail closed.

| Case | Grid | Bits | M(e) | M(e + grid) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1672](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1672) native | 1e-70 | 360 | below 1 | above 1 |
| [1672](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1672) conservative | 1e-70 | 360 | below 1 | above 1 |
| [1928](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1928) native | 1e-10000 | 33347 | below 1 | above 1 |
| [1928](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1928) conservative | 1e-10000 | 33347 | below 1 | above 1 |

Also checked:

- For both models, the 1e-70 endpoints equal the 1e-70 floors of the 1e-10000 endpoints.
- At both heads, 249 gauge44 calls and 417 extra calls with their per-call profiles, plus 22,748 idle rank-48 children, sum to the global profile. Rank mass is 4,816,512 and the deficit is 23,680.
- The headline κ of [PR 1928](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1928) is 2.003e-10010 below its native endpoint, as its choice of b implies. [PR 1672](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1672)'s is 2.817e-6 below.
- Ten semantic controls are rejected: next and previous grid point as endpoint, one child moved from rank 1 to rank 2, m = 72, W − 1, and the surcharge omitted or added in the wrong model. Three are repeated at 1e-10000.

The optional `crosscheck_decimal.py` repeats the 1e-10000 case with Python's `decimal` ln and exp at 10,060 digits. It agrees on all seven log enclosures and all four signs. It takes about 4 minutes and corroborates the result; it is not a certificate.

**No discrepancy was found.**

### Reproduce

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/t74-k554-root-enclosure --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/t74-k554-root-enclosure
```

Local results on Windows, Python 3.12, stdlib only:

```
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
PASS_T74_K554_ROOT_ENCLOSURE_INDEPENDENT | brackets 4 | nesting 2 | controls 10 rejected | 13.5 s
Ran 10 tests ... OK
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/t74-k554-root-enclosure outcome=completed
PASS_DECIMAL_CROSSCHECK | 7 log enclosures | 4 moment signs agree
PASS_INPUTS_MATCH_PINNED_PR_HEADS
```

`tests.test_research_onboarding`, `tests.test_research_replay_selection` and `tests.test_research_assignment` also pass (32 tests). `make` is not installed on this host, so no make target was run. Hosted CI has not run.

### Scope

This is a finite check of recorded endpoints and of the profile arithmetic. The following are taken as given:

- the profiles themselves;
- the native, surcharge-free complex recurrence;
- the outer reduction from b to κ, the fine source-prime padding and the ε → 1 transfer (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1797 audits the [PR 1786](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1786) lemmas on a different supplier);
- all inherited all-size/compiler, realization, hosting, precision/tape, recovery, analytic and bit H1-H5 assumptions.

No new κ is claimed and the selected record is unchanged.

### Open next questions

1. Does [PR 1928](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1928)'s `outer/LEDGER.json` follow from this endpoint, checked by code that does not import `outer/*.py`?
2. Does the global profile equal the profile emitted by the T74 template and owner map? The seed78 emitted-ledger rebuild could be adapted to the two-provider layout.

Workflow feedback: the overlap search finds claims by κ digits but not "who has independently checked this number". A per-claim "independent checks" field in the PR ledger would have saved most of the 30-minute survey.
